tagline: Twelve miles up a glacier's U into the Ruby Mountains.
intro: Out of Lamoille, a valley a settler named after his native Vermont, the road turns up into Lamoille Canyon, the largest valley in the Ruby Mountains. It climbs from about 6,100 feet at the canyon mouth, through a narrow slot and past Lamoille Falls, to 8,800 feet at Road's End.

Glaciers did the carving. They left the canyon a U in cross section, with four hanging valleys high on the side of Thomas Peak, 11,325 feet. At Road's End the driving stops and the 38-mile Ruby Crest Trail begins.

moments.title: Powerhouse Picnic Area
moments.text: At the canyon mouth, a powerhouse built in 1913 for the Elko-Lamoille Power Company burned in 1971 and left only its foundation.

moments.title: Terraces Picnic Area
moments.text: A dense stand of aspens beside Lamoille Creek, where fly-fishermen work the water for brook and wild rainbow trout.

moments.title: Road's End
moments.text: The high point of the road at 8,800 feet, where the canyon swings around Thomas Peak and a short trail starts up to Island Lake in one of the hanging valleys.

practical: One section of Lamoille Canyon Road is a single lane.
